odia: ଷାଠିଏ କାହାଣ ତଣ୍ଡକୁ ଅଛି, ହରି ଭଗତିକି କଡ଼ାଏ ନାହିଁ
title: Plenty for penalties, nothing for devotion
literal_meaning: There are sixty kahans for penalties, but not a small cowrie amount for devotion to Hari.
explanation: The verse sets a large expense beside a tiny amount refused. Its religious contrast is explicit: money can be found for a penalty or an expense one is forced to bear, yet none is available for devotion to Hari. The dictionary’s separate definition of taṇḍa includes fines and compelled expenditure; it does not tell us what offence, if any, lies behind this line. Our reading hears a reproach about priorities, made memorable by the unequal sums. That reading preserves the devotional voice without making spending on worship a test of anyone’s goodness.
meaning_odia: ତଣ୍ଡ ପାଇଁ ବଡ଼ ଅଙ୍କର ଧନ ଅଛି, ହରିଙ୍କ ଭକ୍ତି ପାଇଁ ଅଳ୍ପଟିଏ ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଅସମାନ ତୁଳନାରେ କଥାର ଖୋଚା। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ତଣ୍ଡର ଅର୍ଥ ଜୋରିମାନାଠାରୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇ କରାଯାଉଥିବା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଅଛି; ଏଠାରେ କେଉଁ ଘଟଣାର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କେଉଁ କାମ ପାଇଁ ଟଙ୍କା ମିଳେ ଓ କେଉଁ କାମ ବେଳେ ଅଭାବ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ସେହି ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ଏହା ପଚାରେ। ମୂଳ କଥାର ଭକ୍ତିଭାବ ରହିଥାଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପୂଜାରେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିବାକୁ ମଣିଷର ଭଲମନ୍ଦର ମାପ କରିବା ଆମର ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: A devotional reproach contrasts large compelled expenses with a small amount withheld.
odia_summary: ବାଧ୍ୟ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ପାଇଁ ବହୁତ, ଭକ୍ତି ପାଇଁ ଅଳ୍ପଟିଏ ନାହିଁ—ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ଏହି ଖୋଚା।
usage_example: Original imagined example: Two friends discuss someone who readily pays repeated late fees but says there is nothing to spare for a small devotional gathering they had promised to support. One quotes the line as a comment on those priorities. The scene is invented and is not a demand that anyone fund religious activity.
cultural_context: The primary headword explains a large sum in an older cowrie vocabulary. The lexical taṇḍa source is context-only, not a second witness of the saying. No exact modern currency conversion, offence, historic event or duty to donate is asserted.
